result.title: World of SWECraft: Agent Collaboration at Scale via Simulated Software Worlds
result.summary: As teams of AI agents take on larger projects and long-standing open problems, agent collaboration offers another dimension for scaling inference-time compute. To understand what makes such collaboration effective and scalable, we develop Software World, a framework for simulating multi-agent coworking in realistic software ecosystems. It comes with a pipeline to create environments of real, interdependent Python packages of different topics, sizes, and dependency structures, which we call software worlds. In a simulation, agents maintain packages in the world with a high-level goal of improving software efficiency, and they are free to discover tasks to work on and collaborate with others. We evaluate agents' work in a world collectively by measuring speedup in hidden dependent packages. The framework allows us to study different elements of collaboration by varying communication, ownership, and resource allocation. We run simulations in three different worlds, totaling more than 10,000 hours of agent work across eight models. Overall, performance improvement scales with inference-time compute, with the best model improving downstream efficiency by up to 31%. We show that most agents can find meaningful tasks via collaboration, but some frontier models can prematurely stop looking for improvements and make little progress. We release the simulation framework and traces to support future studies of agent collaboration at https://szj.io/sw.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出 Software World 模拟框架，用真实且相互依赖的 Python 包构成「软件世界」，让多个 agent 自主发现任务并协作提升下游包效率，通过改变通信、归属与资源分配来研究协作要素，并在三个世界上用八种模型运行逾万小时，观察到性能随推理期计算量提升，也发现部分前沿模型会过早停止寻找改进。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 主线无直接关联，但其中「过早停止搜索改进」的失败模式与推理期计算分配、何时终止决策具体相关，可供核查其对 THINK/LOOK/STOP 中停止策略与动态计算的启发。
